name: r6-account
statement: On MATH-500 the problems that an RL-side model gets right and the base side gets wrong (grader v3, cap hits wrong) are split by six ordered rules. The rules read the base row and three independent cued-base T 1.0 samples (kB). (1) Loop: the base hits the cap inside a rule-A repeat. (2) Budget: the base hits the cap with no loop. (3) Answer-statement: the base writes no answer line, or states the gold and then ends on another value. (4) Slip: kB = 3. (5) Sharpening: kB = 1-2. (6) Reach: kB = 0. Two cued-base draws already trade about 28 problems. The null (T1 against a fourth cued sample) is predicted at loop / budget / answer / slip / sharpening / reach = 0 / 0.11 / 0.035 / 0.22 / 0.52 / 0.115. Against the final RL at T 1.0 (fit 0 / 0.25 / 0.03 / 0.18 / 0.44 / 0.10), only budget exceeds the null. So at AI2's setting RL adds a policy of finishing long problems before the cap, plus a larger gap of the same resample kind (one difficulty axis, fewer lost problems). Predicted shares in the other cells: (a) top-8 RL-direction edit: 0 / 0.17 / 0.034 / 0.19 / 0.47 / 0.136, with budget above the null and the rest at the null. (b) Min-p 0.1 at T 1.0, base against RL: 0.37 / 0.21 / 0.03 / 0.12 / 0.21 / 0.06. Truncation locks the base into loops that RL escapes. (c) RL step 400 with the cue at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95: 0.55 / 0.15 / 0.017 / 0.09 / 0.15 / 0.043. (d) The 3.0 first release with the cue at T 0.6: 0.58 / 0.15 / 0.015 / 0.085 / 0.13 / 0.04. (e) The plain base against RL: 0 / 0.045 / 0.38 / 0.38 / 0.165 / 0.03. Which parts exceed the null: budget in every RL-side cell; loop only under truncating samplers, where the base sampler fails and the RL side escapes; answer-statement and slip only against the plain base, where they are the work of the cue (the RL opening), not of later RL training. The largest part still open at T 1.0 is sharpening. A base-only vote over more samples recovers part of it (predicted 456/500).

parts.name: loop
parts.mechanism: Under a truncating sampler (top-p 0.95 at T 0.6, min-p 0.1 at T 1.0), the base's repeat probabilities lock and it loops to the cap on problems it can otherwise finish; the RL side escapes. Carried from r7-account, whose loop shares held in every T 0.6 cell. Graveyard r2-external-2 was refuted by a rule-A count at min-p 0.1 (claimed 2, measured 34). That test refuted 'min-p removes loops', the opposite of what this part asserts, so it does not apply.
parts.rule: The base row is a cap hit, and rule A (an 8,000-character window starting at a line start, zlib ratio < 0.10) fires on its text.

parts.name: budget
parts.mechanism: On long problems the base writes past the budget without solving or committing. RL, trained with truncated rollouts as negatives, solves and finishes them. This revives graveyard r1-across-2 and r1-surprises-1, which were refuted on a theta1.5 answer count and a hard328 pass@4 count. Neither test is about which stored problems hit the cap, so they do not apply.
parts.rule: Not taken earlier, and the base row is a cap hit.

parts.name: answer-statement
parts.mechanism: The base finishes without an answer line, or states the gold and then ends on another value. Graveyard r4-m11 was refuted on first-marker regrades. This rule also takes the no-answer-line form, which that test did not measure.
parts.rule: Not taken earlier. On the normalised lines of the base text: no line holds a box or starts with 'Answer:'; or some line boxes the normalised gold, or equals 'Answer:' + gold. Missing text is taken.

parts.name: slip
parts.mechanism: The base solves the problem in all three independent cued samples, so the miss is a rare sample-specific slip. RL's slip hazard is lowest on such easy problems. This revives graveyard r2-revise-2 and r3-surprises-1, which were refuted on vote@4 and tie-break counts: claims about vote procedures, not about how independent samples classify a gap problem.

parts.name: sharpening
parts.mechanism: The base solves the problem in one or two of three samples; RL concentrates probability on a path the base already samples. The graveyard note is the same as for slip.
parts.rule: Not taken earlier, and kB is 1 or 2.

parts.name: reach
parts.mechanism: No independent cued sample solves the problem, and the RL side reaches a path the base rarely samples. Graveyard r5-m06 was refuted because the base's rate on such problems was higher than it claimed. This part asserts no rate.

scope: MATH-500 only, seven cells. They span three samplings (T 1.0 / top-p 1.0; T 1.0 / min-p 0.1; T 0.6 / top-p 0.95) and these model pairs: final RL (claimed), plain base, top-8 RL-direction weight edit, RL step 400 (standing for the intermediate checkpoints), and the 3.0 first release; the null is a second cued sample. Every gap is reported gross and net. hard328 is left out because the evidence set (three independent cued T 1.0 base samples) is not readable there: the 4-sample rows of result-1dedfe (sameraslan-1114-145237-d124, -145241-fee9, -145246-73ad, -145251-9228) and abaybektursun-1114-200457-e8e6 sit in other workspaces. This removes the hard328 Code-RL and theta cells. MATH-500 Code-RL (abaybektursun-1114-162452-0203), the theta blends (-152855-683b and the other day1_wdiff jobs) and the random-direction cell (-153047-6429) are not readable. No per-problem rows of the 3.0 models other than the first release (the reward5 runs) are listed in inventory.md.

imports.finding: RLVR raises pass@1 by concentrating on paths the base already samples; per-problem coverage at large k barely changes.
imports.how: Grounds the sharpening part as the largest finished-problem part, with a small reach part.

imports.finding: At loop onset, entropy drops toward 0 and the top logit jumps; loop rate falls with temperature.
imports.how: A truncating sampler removes the residual escape mass, so the loop part fills only in the min-p and top-p 0.95 cells.

imports.finding: Temperature changes which problems get a correct trace, not mean accuracy.
imports.how: The basis of the null: two base draws trade problems at equal accuracy, mostly sharpening problems.

explains.quote: At T 1.0 rule A finds 0 loops in T1, T2 and T3
explains.how: The loop part is 0 by construction in the null, RL, plain and top-8 cells.

explains.quote: Truncating the tail at T 1.0 brings loops back
explains.how: The min-p cell has a large loop part at T 1.0.

explains.quote: most of the RL direction's gain is 24 fewer lost problems, not more fixed ones
explains.how: The RL cell's finished-problem composition sits at the null; RL adds gap size and the budget part.

explains.quote: in the class 'other three right' the base fails 7.2%, RL 0.9%
explains.how: This is the slip part (kB = 3), about a fifth of both the null and the RL gap.

explains.quote: its cap hits on the 328 are failures to solve, not failures to stop
explains.how: Budget problems are long unsolved problems that RL solves, not stopping failures.

explains.quote: 16 cap hits with no loop, 14 misread
explains.how: Budget is exactly the 16 T1 cap hits (0.246).

explains.quote: v1/v2 found no answer in 166 of 500 plain-base T 1.0 answers
explains.how: This is the large answer-statement part in the plain-base cell.

conflicts.quote: a removed loop is one more draw at a hard problem
conflicts.how: If loop problems were simply hard, a T 1.0 sample would solve few of them; the account predicts it solves most loop-part gap problems (cross-prediction 1).
Code-RL rescues the base's cap hits on hard328 at half its rate on finished-wrong problems. So a budget part above the null may be specific to Math-RL rather than to RL directions in general.

rival: The strongest rival is one difficulty axis plus the sampler (result-5da8a9): loop and budget are just ways a hard problem fails. Under it, the cued base's untruncated T1 sample solves min-p loop-part gap problems at about its rate on base cap hits (~0.40), and at the same rate as on budget-part problems. This account predicts 0.70 on loop problems and 0.28 on budget problems. The separating number is that T1 solve rate on the min-p loop part (and its difference from the budget part, +0.42 here against about 0 under the rival).

R3 answer-statement: N deletes whitespace, '$', '*', '#', '\left', '\right' and maps '\dfrac', '\tfrac' to '\frac'; g = N(gold); taken if no N(line) contains '\boxed{' and none starts with 'Answer:', or some N(line) contains '\boxed{'+g+'}' or equals 'Answer:'+g or 'Answer:'+g+'.'; missing text is taken. R4 slip: kB == 3. R5 sharpening: kB in {1,2}. R6 reach: kB == 0. Else unassigned. Statistic: loop-part problems / gap problems.

predictions.experiment: Base-only route to the sharpening part, a vote over 9 cued-base samples. Generate one new sample: allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B @ a81bae42, cue prefill [1584, 2268, 33413], all 500 MATH-500 problems, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, max 16,384, seed 11,000,000 + problem_index, no restarts, via studies/rlneurons/jobs/run_cell.py (about 35 H100 minutes). The 9 answers per problem: the 4 attempt-0 samples of day1_3 math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (extracted_v3), T1.jsonl (v3 extraction of its text), the cued-base frustea cells 456c, e383 and b614 (extracted_v3, first row), and the new sample. Each finished, non-empty answer casts one vote. Answers are grouped as equal by rln4_lib.agree; the plurality group wins, and a tie goes to the group holding the shortest finished sample (fewest n_new). The chosen answer is graded with v3; a problem with no vote is wrong.
